column3: Direct parallel: repeats يُحَادُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ and supplies فِى ٱلْأَذَلِّينَ.
Links أَنزَلَ and يَكْفُرْ with a consequential عَذَاب, reinforcing the signs-and-rejection sequence.
Closely parallels crossing حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ and joins disobedience to عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ.
Parallel offense against ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ with the same عَذَابًا مُّهِينًا outcome.
Immediate context names حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ and ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ before 58:5's opposition.
Nearby continuation connects obstruction from سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ with عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ.
Combines denial of مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ with عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ, but lacks the boundary-opposition wording.
Immediate context establishes the contested speech that 58:3-5 regulates.
Pairs fabricated revelation and disdain for ءَايَٰتِهِ with عَذَابَ ٱلْهُونِ; a secondary humiliation parallel.
Pairs ءَايَٰتٍ مُّبَيِّنَٰتٍ with examples of those مِن قَبْلِكُمْ, both explicit in 58:5.
Directly supports the function of أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتٍ بَيِّنَٰتٍ in 58:5.
Near-verbatim parallel to يُحَادِدِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ, with a grave disgrace outcome.
Shares يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ ... ءَايَاتِهِ but adds little to opposition or abasement.
Immediate sequel supplies resurrection, accounting, and witness to 58:5's threat.
Illustrates refusal of بَيِّنَة and declared non-belief, though the terms differ.
Directly joins ءَايَٰتٍ بَيِّنَٰتٍ to rejection, sharpening 58:5's final clause.
Nearby context about the messenger and disciplined approach, but no direct 58:5 vocabulary.
A secondary contrast of human خصيم مُّبِين with manifest signs; limited payoff.
Direct pairing of rejection/denial of ءَايَٰت and عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ.
Offers the inverse relation: rescue from ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ, not its cause.
Frames denial while witnessing ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ; supports the disclosed-signs dimension.
Makes those مِن قَبْلِهِم a precedent of destruction, useful for كَمَا كُبِتَ.
Immediate setup to 58:4-5: correction, admonition, and divine knowledge.
Supports the تَنزِيل source of the signs, but not their rejection or punishment.
A speech-boundary instruction with punishment; only a distant contextual parallel.
Pairs intensified punishment with مُهَانًا, a secondary counterpart to مُّهِين.
Reinforces تَنزِيل as authoritative source, but remains general.
Another explicit ءَايَٰتٍ مُّبَيِّنَٰتٍ formulation, adding guidance as a parallel reading.
Immediate continuation grounds later disclosure of deeds; complementary rather than repetitive.
The non-denial of good deeds is only a lexical opposite to 58:5's كفر.
Joins ءَايَٰتٌ بَيِّنَٰتٌ to جحود, but omits abasement and opposition.
Directly combines extended reprieve, كفر, and عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ; clarifies a possible temporal pattern.
Its V12 route is contrast-only and the text adds no direct 58:5 relation.
Uses يَكْبِتَهُمْ and reversal after disbelief; directly illuminates كُبِتُوا despite different setting.
Nearby sequel on oath and false self-assessment, extending the opposing party's profile.
Names حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ and their explanation, but applies a separate legal boundary.
Shows communal separation from denial and mockery of ءَايَٰت; indirect to 58:5.
Precedes 5:115's requested sign; useful only with that adjacent candidate.
The light/darkness frame and كفر are broad and not localized to 58:5's sequence.
Only supplies the كَمَا ... مِن قَبْلِكُمْ pattern in a different practice.
Nearby instance of repeated prohibition and معصية ٱلرَّسُول with punishment.
Connects mockery of ءَايَات to عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ, a clear humiliation parallel.
Directly repeats يـنزل ... ءَايَٰتٍ بَيِّنَٰتٍ and adds an exit-path parallel.
Provides a return-to-offense pattern and enclosing consequence; indirect but relevant boundary evidence.
The V12 link is contrast-only and no direct vocabulary or structure is shared.
Affirms what was أَنزَلْنَا and ٱلْحَقّ, but offers no rejection or consequence parallel.
Provides the channel's reduction/erasure pattern for believers and rejecters, indirectly related to كُبِتُوا.
Substantive حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ parallel, though its legal scene is distant from 58:5.
Preceding opponents and their outcome echo the historical comparison only broadly.
Nearby fire consequence for the same local opposing group; adds finality, not the key terms.
Supports the repeated تَنزِيل source of 58:5's signs, without further overlap.
General believer/disbeliever contrast and fire outcome; little specific contribution.
Establishes messenger roles, but does not clarify opposition, signs, or abasement.
The only V12 relation is contrast; no direct link to 58:5's phrasing.
Pairs prior exemplars with severe punishment; supports the كَمَا كُبِتَ historical warning.
Immediate continuation asserts victory for Allah and His messengers over the opposition of 58:5.
Positive counterpart to 4:14's حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ; useful as a secondary boundary contrast.
Broad post-grace كفر formulation, without the signs, opposition, or abasement structure.
Nearby classification and loss of the local opponents, complementary to 58:5.
Its V12 relation is contrast-only; the remaining overlap is too general.
No direct lexical, channel, or V12 relation to 58:5.
Previous messengers mocked, reprieve, then seizure: a historical consequence parallel.
Supports protected authoritative تَنزِيل, but not 58:5's rejection and humiliation.
Shows resistance to clear ءَايَات and refusal to alter the revealed message.
Illustrates rejecting a more guided messenger-message, a secondary opposition parallel.
Redundant general تَنزِيل formula; adds little after stronger parallels.
Explicitly joins كفر, حُدُود, and what is أَنزَلَ on the messenger, though without humiliation.
Channel relation concerns an unrelated purity reading; no textual payoff for 58:5.
A secondary reflection on claimed إهانة, not 58:5's punitive مُّهِين.
Directly repeats حَآدَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ and gives the contrary affiliation/outcome.
Inherited imitation parallels resistance only at a high level.
Combines حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ, clarification, and a prior-example formula in a distinct legal scene.
No meaningful lexical, channel, or V12 connection remains.
Channel relation is unrelated to 58:5; no direct textual overlap.
General عذاب of disbelievers after divine intervention; limited relation to 58:5.
No direct lexical, channel, or V12 connection to 58:5.
Channel-level opposition resonance only; the text does not explain 58:5's terms.
General تَنزِيل of the book is redundant after closer sign parallels.
Revelation and devoted response offer only a broad contrast to 58:5.
Non-erasure and recording of deeds weakly complements 58:6, not 58:5 itself.
No direct lexical, channel, or V12 connection to 58:5.
Contrasts broad submission with those for whom punishment and humiliation obtain; secondary support.
Shares كافرين and عذاب مُّهِين but its concealment scene is otherwise separate.
The V12 link is only mixed and the text has no specific 58:5 relation.
Close parallel to opposition against Allah and messenger, with severe punishment.
Pairs established كفر with عذاب مُّهِين; broad but clear outcome parallel.
Explicitly joins clear guidance, opposition to the messenger, and failed deeds.
Pairs imposed ordinance with ءَايَٰتٍ بَيِّنَٰتٍ; clarifies the disclosed-boundary side of 58:5.
False dealing with Allah and messenger plus disbeliever punishment, but no close wording.
Offers a pride-and-kufr pattern that supports opposition as a stance, secondarily.
Opposition to messenger and truth is present, but the scene is not punitive or explanatory of 58:5.
General أَنزَلْنَٰهُ and warning formula; redundant to stronger تَنزِيل cards.
Direct historical-precedent frame, explicit messengers, and بَيِّنَٰت; useful for كَمَا كُبِتَ.
Directly supports the disclosure aspect of ءَايَٰتٍ بَيِّنَٰتٍ, though very general.
No direct lexical, channel, or V12 relation to 58:5.
Messenger as مُنذِرٌ مُّبِينٌ broadly complements the manifest-signs clause.
No usable direct relation beyond a general mention of كافرين.
A secondary pattern of belief followed by كفر and blocked understanding; not 58:5's opposition.
Generic أَنزَلْنَا and شرك offer no specific contribution.
General نزول and divergent reception is a remote parallel, with no boundary or abasement detail.
Near-exact parallel: شَآقُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ, followed by severe consequence.
Explicit opposition to ٱلرَّسُول after تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ directly complements 58:5.
Directly joins أَنزَلَ and كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ with عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ.
Compact parallel of كذبوا بآياتنا and enduring fire, without the boundary wording.
Rejection of ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ and a promised عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ reinforce the punitive pattern.
Explicit كفروا بآياتنا with recurring punishment; relevant but less specific than the humiliation cards.
Denial of ءَايَٰتِنا and the fire outcome offer a general consequence parallel.
Denial of ٱلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ provides a close reception-of-revelation parallel.
كذبوا بآياتنا and استكبروا عنها link denial and arrogant stance to enduring fire.
Active turning from ءَايَٰتِى and denial of them develops the resistant-reading side of 58:5.
Earlier peoples, clear messengers, rejection, and consequence closely support كَمَا كُبِتَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ.
Directly pairs non-belief in ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ with punishment, though without opposition terminology.
كفروا بآياتنا followed by a defined recompense supports the signs-and-consequence sequence.
Denial of ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِم is joined to nullified deeds; a secondary consequence parallel.
Reception of ءَايَٰت followed by disregard and a corresponding outcome offers a close structural parallel.
Those who strive ضدّ ءَايَٰتِنا are assigned the fire, strongly illuminating active resistance.
Explicit ءَايَٰتِنا بَيِّنَٰتٍ and visible hostile response provide a close reception parallel.
Links the end of earlier wrongdoers to denial and mockery of ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ.
Turning away after being reminded by ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِ is a direct resistance-and-retribution parallel.
Active striving against ءَايَٰتِنا and a painful punishment closely match 58:5's opposition pattern.
The seizure of earlier rejecters supplies additional historical-precedent evidence.
Argument against ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ without authority gives a direct, though non-identical, opposition pattern.
Repeated جدال في ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ makes the resistance to disclosed signs explicit.
Those who deviate regarding ءَايَٰتِنا form a relevant alternative description of opposition.
Directly links كفروا بآيات ربهم to عَذَابٌ مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ.
Clear recited ءَايَٰتُنَا and the rejecters' dismissive response closely complement 58:5.
An earlier people denied and rejected the messenger; useful precedent evidence for كَمَا كُبِتَ.
Directly combines كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا with an enduring fire consequence.
Concise direct stance: كَانَ لِـَٔايَٰتِنَا عَنِيدًا, highly relevant to resisting manifest signs.
Intensive denial of ءَايَٰتِنا contributes to the rejection side, but lacks the boundary and messenger terms.
Messengers, بَيِّنَٰت, and the revealed الكتاب/ميزان make this a major parallel to 58:5's disclosed authority.
A messenger recites ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ مُبَيِّنَٰتٍ, directly joining messenger and manifest signs.
Links what is أَنزَلَ to the messenger's تبيين; it supports 58:5's بَيِّنَٰت clause.
Makes the revealed كتاب an instrument of تبيين amid disagreement; a secondary clarification parallel.
Describes the revealed كتاب as تِبْيَانًا, supporting the disclosure dimension without opposition terms.
Pairs a divine برهان with a descended نُورًا مُّبِينًا, a close but non-identical signs parallel.
The coming messenger who يبين after concealment complements the reveal-versus-covering pattern.
Connects sent prophets, the revealed كتاب, and judgment amid dispute; broad background for the messenger-sign relation.
Explicitly assigns each messenger the task of تبيين, providing a complementary reading of manifest signs.
